correctness.rationale: The original lower-bound proof omitted the case where tau(n)<209 is a prime at least 19. The corrected proof now excludes every prime value tau(n)=r uniformly: tau(n)=r forces n=a^(r-1), r does not divide a, and Fermat gives n congruent to 1 mod r, contradicting Q(n) congruent to 0 mod r because Q(1)=1. For composite tau(n)<209, all prime factors below 19 except 11 are excluded by the quadratic-residue check; any factor at least 19 would force a remaining factor at least 11 and hence tau(n)>=209, so the sole composite possibility is 121, which the existing Fermat argument excludes. The 209 construction was independently replayed and the source family remains valid.
risks: The repair changes only the proof; the theorem statement and construction are unchanged.
